items.headline: Stocks slip Tuesday as Nvidia sinks and hot inflation lifts rate-hike bets
items.note: The Dow fell 0.3% to 52,231.89, the S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq fell 0.74% to 25,065.87, giving back part of Monday's big rally. Nvidia was the biggest drag, and the October inflation report weighed too.

items.headline: October consumer prices rose 0.4%, hotter than expected
items.note: Economists expected 0.3%. Core prices (excluding food and energy) rose 0.3% versus 0.2% expected. September's headline reading was 0.6%, so inflation cooled but not by enough. The BLS did not publish an annual rate because of the 2025 shutdown data gap.

items.headline: Fed now seen hiking in December; a half-point hike gets 11% odds
items.note: CME FedWatch showed an 88% chance of a quarter-point hike on Dec. 8-9 and 11% for a half-point, up from zero a week ago. Fed Governor Waller said he would back 50 basis points if inflation ran hot. Higher rates generally pressure growth and tech stocks.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield jumps to 4.992% after a weak bond auction
items.note: The 10-year briefly topped 5% and the 2-year rose to 4.736%. A $42 billion 10-year note sale was soft, with dealers left holding about 10% of it, the most since May. Falling oil prices offset some of the pressure.

items.headline: Nvidia falls 5.5% as the Jensen Huang probe extends a two-day slide
items.note: Shares have dropped for two days on reports about CEO Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese intelligence link, which Nvidia's board is investigating. As the largest AI chip company, its stock swings move the whole Nasdaq.

items.headline: Anthropic sets IPO range at $70-$78 a share, trading expected Nov. 19
items.note: The range implies a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, down from the $2 trillion once floated. Pricing is planned for Nov. 18 on the Nasdaq under ticker ANT, with about 20% of shares aimed at retail investors. It is a big test of public-market appetite for AI companies.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Ember, a cheap model for high-volume agent work
items.note: Meta priced it at $0.10 per million input tokens and says it undercuts Anthropic's Haiku and OpenAI's Luna. It handles text, images and audio, and is meant to run tasks planned by Meta's larger Muse Wonder. Cheap small models are what make agent products affordable to build.

items.headline: OpenAI launches business profiles in ChatGPT and buys travel startup Odessia
items.note: The Business Hub beta lets companies build profiles and agents inside ChatGPT, similar to Google's business listings. OpenAI also acquired Odessia, an AI travel agent, and its founder is joining; terms weren't disclosed.

learn.explain: The U.S. government borrows money by selling Treasury bonds and notes at auctions, where big dealers and investors bid for them. If demand is weak, buyers demand a higher yield, so the price falls and the yield rises. On Tuesday a $42 billion 10-year note sale was soft, with dealers stuck holding about 10% of it, the most since May. That pushed the 10-year yield to 4.992%. Because mortgages, corporate loans and stock valuations are all tied to Treasury yields, a weak auction can ripple through the whole market.
